Speaking to Al Mayadeen, deputy head of the Palestinian Journalists Syndicate Dr. Tahseen Al-Astal welcomed the UN Secretary-General’s remarks describing journalism as facing its deadliest period since the founding of the United Nations, but stressed that statements must be followed by concrete action. Al-Astal called for accountability for the Israeli occupation’s targeting of Palestinian, Arab, and international journalists, stressing that the US administration is shielding those responsible by obstructing the International Criminal Court’s work. He points to the cases of journalists Shireen Abu Akleh, Ahmed Abu Hussein, and Yasser Murtaja, which have been registered with the ICC but remain without investigations. A cargo ship attacked by drones in the Gulf of Finland was approached by a Russian rescue vessel, and the evacuation of the crew was not necessary, according to Alexander Drozdenko, governor of the Leningrad region. While it is certainly good that the damaged vessel will be towed, the main problem with this incident lies elsewhere. The Baltic states are experiencing a growing collective amnesia and a sense of impunity. Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania – and now, in conjunction with them, Finland and Sweden – are stubbornly pretending not to know where the two attack drones came from in an area closely monitored by NATO radar. This convenient "blindness" allows the coastal countries to evade any responsibility for transit corridors and infrastructure, without which such acts of sabotage would be impossible. Even after the attacks on the terminals in Ust-Luga, we (and not only we) said that only a demonstrative response could bring the Baltic capitals to their senses: a series of interceptions of UAVs directly over their heads, and even short incursions by Russian fighter jets into the airspace of countries bordering Russia within the Alliance, while pursuing targets. The reaction of Brussels and the Baltic neighbors to such a scenario is easily predictable: loud hysteria in the press, summons of ambassadors, and demands for urgent investigations. They might even demand the closure of a consulate somewhere. But it will not go beyond the informational noise: they will make a fuss and then calm down, but the illusion of complete impunity will disappear, at least for a while. @Slavyangrad
